title: 美国专利审查程序手册（MPEP）节选
titleEn: Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) — selected sections
version: 第 9 版 Rev. 01.2024（2024 年 11 月发布，现行版）
note: MPEP 不是法律，是 USPTO 给审查员的操作手册；法院不受其约束。Rev. 01.2024 之后 USPTO 又发过若干备忘录（如 2025 年 IPR 立案改由局长决定、2025-12 Ex parte Desjardins 关于 §101），以 USPTO 网站为准。

paras.en: During patent examination, the pending claims must be “given their broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification.”
paras.zh: 在专利审查中，待审权利要求必须“在与说明书一致的前提下给予最宽合理解释”。

explain.en: BRI applies only to pending claims at the USPTO. Courts construe issued claims under Phillips, which can be narrower. That is why MPEP § 2173.02 says examination applies a “lower threshold for ambiguity” than a court.
explain.zh: BRI 只用于 USPTO 审查中的权利要求；法院解释已授权权利要求用 Phillips 标准，范围可能更窄。所以 MPEP § 2173.02 说审查阶段对“不清楚”的门槛比法院更低。

explain.en: China has no separate label, but the Examination Guidelines read claims in light of the description in the same spirit. In English you can say: “The claim is given its broadest reasonable interpretation in light of the description.”
explain.zh: 中国没有单独的名称，但审查指南同样结合说明书理解权利要求。英文可以写：The claim is given its broadest reasonable interpretation in light of the description.

paras.en: To reject a claim as anticipated by a reference, the disclosure must teach every element required by the claim under its broadest reasonable interpretation.
paras.zh: 要以一份文献“预见”为由驳回权利要求，该文献必须教导了权利要求在最宽合理解释下所需的每一个要素。

paras.en: “A claim is anticipated only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference.”
paras.zh: “只有当权利要求记载的每一个要素都在单独一份现有技术文献中被明确或固有地描述时，该权利要求才被预见。”

explain.en: This is the US version of China’s “single comparison” rule (Part II, Chapter 3, § 3.1(2)). “Anticipated by” is the standard verb: “Claim 1 is anticipated by D1.”
explain.zh: 这就是美国版的“单独对比原则”（中国指南第二部分第三章 3.1 节（2））。anticipated by 是固定搭配：Claim 1 is anticipated by D1。

explain.en: “Inherently” matters: a feature not written in the reference can still anticipate if it is necessarily present (see MPEP § 2112).
explain.zh: 注意 inherently（固有地）：文献没写明但必然存在的特征也能构成预见，见 MPEP § 2112。

units.label: MPEP § 2131.02
units.title: Genus and species
units.titleZh: 上位与下位（通式与具体化合物）

paras.en: “A generic claim cannot be allowed to an applicant if the prior art discloses a species falling within the claimed genus.”
paras.zh: “如果现有技术公开了落入所要求保护的上位范围内的一个下位种，就不能向申请人授予该上位权利要求。”

paras.en: A genus does not always anticipate a claim to a species within the genus. However, when the species is clearly named, the species claim is anticipated no matter how many other species are additionally named.
paras.zh: 上位概念并不总能预见其范围内的下位权利要求。但如果该下位种被明确点名，无论同时还列出了多少其他下位种，该下位权利要求都被预见。

paras.en: If one of ordinary skill in the art is able to “at once envisage” the specific compound within the generic chemical formula, the compound is anticipated.
paras.zh: 如果本领域普通技术人员能够从通式中“立即想到”该具体化合物，则该化合物被预见。

explain.en: Same direction as China Part II Ch. 3 § 3.2.2 and Ch. 10 § 5.1(2): a species destroys the genus; a genus alone does not destroy a species. The US adds the “at once envisage” exception: a small, well-delineated genus can anticipate a species.
explain.zh: 与中国第二部分第三章 3.2.2 节、第十章 5.1 节（2）方向一致：下位破坏上位，上位本身不破坏下位。美国多了“at once envisage”例外：范围很小、取代基界定清楚的通式可以预见具体化合物。

explain.en: Useful phrases: “a species anticipates the genus”; “the claimed species is not specifically disclosed”; “cannot be at once envisaged from the generic formula”.
explain.zh: 常用表达：a species anticipates the genus（下位破坏上位）；the claimed species is not specifically disclosed（未具体公开）；cannot be at once envisaged from the generic formula（不能从通式中直接想到）。

paras.en: When the prior art discloses a range which touches or overlaps the claimed range, but no specific examples falling within the claimed range are disclosed, a case by case determination must be made as to anticipation.
paras.zh: 当现有技术公开的范围与要求保护的范围相接或重叠、但没有公开落入要求保护范围内的具体实例时，是否构成预见必须个案判断。

paras.en: In order to anticipate the claims, the claimed subject matter must be disclosed in the reference with “sufficient specificity to constitute an anticipation under the statute.”
paras.zh: 要构成预见，要求保护的主题必须在文献中以“足以构成法定预见的具体程度”被公开。

explain.en: A real difference from China. Under Part II Ch. 3 § 3.2.4(2), a partly overlapping range or a common end point destroys novelty. The US asks for “sufficient specificity” instead, and an overlap usually goes to § 103 (MPEP § 2144.05).
explain.zh: 这是中美的实质差异。中国第二部分第三章 3.2.4 节（2）：范围部分重叠或有共同端点即破坏新颖性。美国要求“sufficient specificity”，重叠通常放到 §103 处理（MPEP § 2144.05）。

explain.en: Both systems agree that a specific value inside the claimed range anticipates it (China § 3.2.4(1)).
explain.zh: 两国一致的是：现有技术的具体数值落在要求保护的范围内，即破坏新颖性（中国 3.2.4 节（1））。

paras.en: “[T]he discovery of a previously unappreciated property of a prior art composition, or of a scientific explanation for the prior art’s functioning, does not render the old composition patentably new to the discoverer.”
paras.zh: “发现现有技术组合物此前未被认识的性质，或对现有技术作用原理给出科学解释，并不能使该旧组合物对发现者而言具备新颖性。”

paras.en: The fact that a certain result or characteristic may occur or be present in the prior art is not sufficient to establish the inherency of that result or characteristic.
paras.zh: 某一结果或特性在现有技术中“可能”出现或存在，不足以证明该结果或特性是固有的。

paras.en: “In relying upon the theory of inherency, the examiner must provide a basis in fact and/or technical reasoning to reasonably support the determination that the allegedly inherent characteristic necessarily flows from the teachings of the applied prior art.”
paras.zh: “依据固有性理论时，审查员必须提供事实依据和/或技术推理，合理支持所称固有特性必然来自所引现有技术的教导这一认定。”

explain.en: Compare China Part II Ch. 3 § 3.2.5 and Ch. 10 § 5.3: when parameters cannot distinguish the product, novelty is presumed lacking and the applicant must prove a difference. The US works the same way: once the examiner gives a reason, the burden shifts to the applicant (§ 2112 V).
explain.zh: 对照中国第二部分第三章 3.2.5 节、第十章 5.3 节：参数无法区分时推定不具备新颖性，由申请人举证不同。美国一样：审查员给出理由后，举证责任转移给申请人（§ 2112 第 V 部分）。

explain.en: Key words: “necessarily” (必然), “may” is not enough; “the burden shifts to the applicant”.
explain.zh: 关键词：necessarily（必然），只是 may（可能）不够；the burden shifts to the applicant（举证责任转移给申请人）。

paras.en: As a result, it is no longer possible to antedate or “swear behind” certain prior art disclosures by making a showing under 37 CFR 1.131 that the inventor invented the claimed subject matter prior to the effective date of the prior art disclosure.
paras.zh: 因此，已经不能再依据 37 CFR 1.131 证明发明人在现有技术公开的有效日之前就完成了发明，从而“追溯在先”某些现有技术公开。

explain.en: AIA (applications with an effective filing date on or after 16 March 2013) moved the US to first-inventor-to-file. Date of invention no longer matters; the effective filing date (actual filing date or the earliest priority/benefit date) does — the same idea as China’s 申请日/优先权日.
explain.zh: AIA（有效申请日在 2013-03-16 及以后的申请）把美国改为“发明人先申请制”。不再看发明日，只看有效申请日（实际申请日或最早的优先权/在先申请日），与中国的申请日/优先权日概念一致。

units.label: MPEP § 2152.02(b)
units.title: What a prior art document must describe
units.titleZh: 现有技术文献需要“描述”到什么程度

paras.en: First, “each and every element of the claimed invention” must be disclosed either explicitly or inherently, and the elements must be “arranged or combined in the same way as in the claim.”
paras.zh: 第一，“要求保护的发明的每一个要素”都必须被明确或固有地公开，并且这些要素必须“以与权利要求相同的方式排列或组合”。

paras.en: Second, a person of ordinary skill in the art must have been enabled to make the invention without undue experimentation.
paras.zh: 第二，本领域普通技术人员必须能够在无需过度实验的情况下制造出该发明。

explain.en: An anticipating reference must be enabling. China reaches a similar result in Ch. 10 § 5.1(1): a compound is not novel when its structure is disclosed, unless the applicant shows it could not be obtained before the filing date.
explain.zh: 构成预见的文献必须“能够实现”。中国第十章 5.1 节（1）结果类似：结构被公开的化合物不具备新颖性，除非申请人证明申请日前无法获得该化合物。

units.label: MPEP § 2153.01(a)
units.title: Grace period (inventor’s own disclosure)
units.titleZh: 宽限期（发明人自己的公开）

paras.en: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A) first provides that a disclosure which would otherwise qualify as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) is excepted as prior art if the disclosure is made: (1) one year or less before the effective filing date of the claimed invention; and (2) by the inventor or a joint inventor or by another who obtained the subject matter disclosed directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor (i.e., an inventor-originated disclosure).
paras.zh: AIA 第 102(b)(1)(A) 条规定，本可构成 102(a)(1) 现有技术的公开，如果满足以下条件则不作为现有技术：（1）发生在要求保护发明的有效申请日之前一年以内；并且（2）由发明人或共同发明人作出，或者由直接或间接从发明人处获得该内容的他人作出（即源自发明人的公开）。

explain.en: Very different from China. China Art. 24 gives six months and only for four listed situations (state emergency, recognized exhibitions, prescribed conferences, disclosure without consent). The US gives one year for any inventor-originated disclosure, including the inventor’s own paper.
explain.zh: 与中国差别很大。中国专利法第 24 条只有六个月，且限于四种情形（紧急状态、指定展览会、规定的学术会议、他人未经同意泄露）。美国对任何源自发明人的公开都给一年，包括发明人自己发表的论文。

explain.en: Phrase: “The publication is excepted as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A).”
explain.zh: 常用表达：The publication is excepted as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A).（该出版物依 102(b)(1)(A) 不作为现有技术。）

units.label: MPEP § 2154.01
units.title: Earlier-filed U.S. patent documents
units.titleZh: 申请在先、公开在后的美国专利文献

paras.en: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) sets forth three types of patent documents that are available as prior art as of the date they were effectively filed with respect to the subject matter relied upon in the document if they name another inventor: (1) U.S. patents; (2) U.S. patent application publications; and (3) certain WIPO published applications.
paras.zh: AIA 第 102(a)(2) 条规定了三类专利文献：如果它们署名的是其他发明人，则就文献中被引用的内容而言，自其有效申请日起即可作为现有技术：（1）美国专利；（2）美国专利申请公布；（3）某些 WIPO 公布的申请。

explain.en: This is roughly China’s 抵触申请 (Art. 22(2)), with two differences: in the US it can also be used for obviousness (§ 103), and in China it only counts for novelty; and the US excludes documents of the same inventor.
explain.zh: 大致相当于中国的抵触申请（第 22 条第 2 款），但有两点不同：美国还可以用来评价显而易见性（§103），中国抵触申请只能评价新颖性；美国排除同一发明人的文献。

paras.en: Obviousness is a question of law based on underlying factual inquiries.
paras.zh: 显而易见性是一个法律问题，但以基础的事实调查为依据。

paras.en: (A) Determining the scope and content of the prior art;
paras.zh: （A）确定现有技术的范围和内容；

paras.en: (B) Ascertaining the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art; and
paras.zh: （B）查明要求保护的发明与现有技术之间的区别；以及

paras.en: (C) Resolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art.
paras.zh: （C）确定相关领域的普通技术水平。

paras.en: Such evidence, sometimes referred to as “secondary considerations,” may include evidence of commercial success, long-felt but unsolved needs, failure of others, and unexpected results.
paras.zh: 这类证据有时称为“辅助考虑因素”，可以包括商业成功、长期存在但未解决的需求、他人的失败以及预料不到的效果。

explain.en: Graham ≈ steps 1 and 2 of China’s three-step test (closest prior art, distinguishing features). China’s step 2 then restates the objective technical problem; the US has no fixed “problem” step and instead asks for a reason to combine (§ 2143).
explain.zh: Graham 大致对应中国“三步法”的前两步（最接近的现有技术、区别特征）。中国第二步还要重新确定“实际解决的技术问题”；美国没有固定的“技术问题”步骤，而是要求说明组合的理由（§ 2143）。

explain.en: The four secondary considerations match China Part II Ch. 4 § 5 almost one to one: long-felt need = 5.1, unexpected results = 5.3, commercial success = 5.4. “Failure of others” has no separate heading in China; “overcoming a technical prejudice” (5.2) is close to US “teaching away”.
explain.zh: 四个辅助因素与中国第二部分第四章第 5 节几乎一一对应：长期需求 = 5.1，预料不到的效果 = 5.3，商业成功 = 5.4。“他人的失败”中国没有单列；“克服技术偏见”（5.2）接近美国的 teaching away。

paras.en: The key to supporting any rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 is the clear articulation of the reason(s) why the claimed invention would have been obvious.
paras.zh: 支持任何 §103 驳回的关键，是清楚地阐明要求保护的发明为什么是显而易见的。

paras.en: “‘[R]ejections on obviousness cannot be sustained by mere conclusory statements; instead, there must be some articulated reasoning with some rational underpinning to support the legal conclusion of obviousness.’”
paras.zh: “‘显而易见性的驳回不能仅靠结论性陈述维持；必须有阐明的、具有合理依据的推理来支持显而易见这一法律结论。’”

paras.en: (A) Combining prior art elements according to known methods to yield predictable results;
paras.zh: （A）按已知方法组合现有技术要素，得到可预期的结果；

paras.en: (B) Simple substitution of one known element for another to obtain predictable results;
paras.zh: （B）用一个已知要素简单替换另一个，得到可预期的结果；

paras.en: (C) Use of known technique to improve similar devices (methods, or products) in the same way;
paras.zh: （C）用已知技术以相同方式改进类似的装置（方法或产品）；

paras.en: (D) Applying a known technique to a known device (method, or product) ready for improvement to yield predictable results;
paras.zh: （D）把已知技术用于有待改进的已知装置（方法或产品），得到可预期的结果；

paras.en: (E) “Obvious to try” – choosing from a finite number of identified, predictable solutions, with a reasonable expectation of success;
paras.zh: （E）“显而易见可尝试”——从有限数量的、已确认的、可预期的方案中选择，并有合理的成功预期；

paras.en: (F) Known work in one field of endeavor may prompt variations of it for use in either the same field or a different one based on design incentives or other market forces if the variations are predictable to one of ordinary skill in the art;
paras.zh: （F）一个领域的已知成果，基于设计动机或其他市场因素，可能促使人们在同一或不同领域对其作出变型，只要这些变型对普通技术人员而言是可预期的；

paras.en: (G) Some teaching, suggestion, or motivation in the prior art that would have led one of ordinary skill to modify the prior art reference or to combine prior art reference teachings to arrive at the claimed invention.
paras.zh: （G）现有技术中存在某种教导、启示或动机（TSM），会促使普通技术人员修改现有技术文献或组合多份文献的教导，从而得到要求保护的发明。

explain.en: (G) TSM is the closest to China’s 技术启示 in step 3. (A) and (B) correspond roughly to China’s 组合发明 (Ch. 4 § 4.2) and 要素替代 (§ 4.6.2). (E) is used a lot in pharma (salts, enantiomers, formulations).
explain.zh: （G）TSM 最接近中国三步法第三步的“技术启示”。（A）（B）大致对应中国的组合发明（第四章 4.2 节）和要素替代的发明（4.6.2 节）。（E）在医药领域用得很多（盐型、对映体、制剂）。

explain.en: When you write in English, avoid “it is obvious” alone; give the reason: “It would have been obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date to …, because …”.
explain.zh: 用英文写时，不要只写 it is obvious，要写出理由：It would have been obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date to …, because …

units.label: MPEP § 2141.03
units.title: Person of ordinary skill in the art

paras.en: The person of ordinary skill in the art is a hypothetical person who is presumed to have known the relevant art at the relevant time.
paras.zh: 本领域普通技术人员是一个假想的人，推定其在相关时间知晓相关领域的技术。

paras.en: “A person of ordinary skill in the art is also a person of ordinary creativity, not an automaton.”
paras.zh: “本领域普通技术人员也是具有普通创造力的人，而不是机器人。”

explain.en: Note the contrast: China Part II Ch. 4 § 2.4 says the person skilled in the art “不具有创造能力” (has no creativity). KSR says the US person has “ordinary creativity”. In practice this makes US obviousness somewhat easier to establish for routine variations.
explain.zh: 注意对比：中国第二部分第四章 2.4 节说本领域技术人员“不具有创造能力”；KSR 说美国的技术人员有“普通创造力”。实际效果是：对常规变型，美国更容易认定显而易见。

explain.en: Terms: US “person having ordinary skill in the art” (PHOSITA/POSA); China’s official law translation uses “person skilled in the relevant field of technology”; “person skilled in the art” is the usual short form.
explain.zh: 术语：美国 person having ordinary skill in the art（简称 PHOSITA/POSA）；中国专利法官方英译用 person skilled in the relevant field of technology；日常写作常用 person skilled in the art。

paras.en: (1) a finding that at the relevant time, there had been a recognized problem or need in the art, which may include a design need or market pressure to solve a problem;
paras.zh: （1）认定在相关时间，本领域存在公认的问题或需求，可以包括解决问题的设计需要或市场压力；

paras.en: (2) a finding that there had been a finite number of identified, predictable potential solutions to the recognized need or problem;
paras.zh: （2）认定针对该需求或问题，存在有限数量的、已确认的、可预期的潜在方案；

paras.en: (3) a finding that one of ordinary skill in the art could have pursued the known potential solutions with a reasonable expectation of success; and
paras.zh: （3）认定普通技术人员可以在有合理成功预期的情况下尝试这些已知方案；以及

paras.en: Thus, Ortho-McNeil helps to clarify the Supreme Court’s requirement in KSR for “a finite number” of predictable solutions when an obvious to try rationale is applied: under the Federal Circuit’s case law “finite” means “small or easily traversed” in the context of the art in question.
paras.zh: 因此，Ortho-McNeil 案帮助澄清了 KSR 中“有限数量”可预期方案的要求：按联邦巡回上诉法院的判例，“有限”是指在相关领域中“数量少或容易逐一尝试”。

explain.en: MPEP § 2143 discusses pharma cases you will meet often: Pfizer v. Apotex (amlodipine besylate, 53 salt-forming anions), Takeda (pioglitazone, no obvious lead compound), Sanofi v. Apotex (clopidogrel enantiomer, unexpected).
explain.zh: MPEP § 2143 讨论了你常会遇到的医药案例：Pfizer v. Apotex（苯磺酸氨氯地平，53 种成盐阴离子）、Takeda（吡格列酮，没有明显的先导化合物）、Sanofi v. Apotex（氯吡格雷对映体，效果预料不到）。

explain.en: China has no “obvious to try” heading. The nearest is Ch. 4 § 4.3 selection inventions: choosing from known possibilities without unexpected effects is not inventive.
explain.zh: 中国没有“显而易见可尝试”的单独标题，最接近的是第四章 4.3 节选择发明：从已知可能性中选择且没有预料不到的效果，则不具备创造性。

paras.en: Where there is a reason to modify or combine the prior art to achieve the claimed invention, the claims may be rejected as prima facie obvious provided there is also a reasonable expectation of success.
paras.zh: 当存在修改或组合现有技术以得到要求保护的发明的理由时，只要同时存在合理的成功预期，即可将权利要求作为表面上显而易见予以驳回。

paras.en: Conclusive proof of efficacy is not required to show a reasonable expectation of success.
paras.zh: 证明合理的成功预期，并不要求确定性的疗效证据。

explain.en: In US pharma practice the fight is often “motivation” plus “reasonable expectation of success”. China’s step 3 has no separate “expectation of success” limb, but arguments that the prior art gives no 技术启示 because the effect was unpredictable play the same role.
explain.zh: 美国医药案件常围绕“动机”加“合理成功预期”两点争论。中国三步法第三步没有单独的“成功预期”要件，但“效果不可预期，因此现有技术没有给出技术启示”的论证起同样作用。

paras.en: In the case where the claimed ranges “overlap or lie inside ranges disclosed by the prior art” a prima facie case of obviousness exists.
paras.zh: 当要求保护的范围“与现有技术公开的范围重叠或落入其中”时，即构成表面上的显而易见。

paras.en: “[W]here the general conditions of a claim are disclosed in the prior art, it is not inventive to discover the optimum or workable ranges by routine experimentation.”
paras.zh: “当权利要求的一般条件已被现有技术公开时，通过常规实验找出最佳或可行的范围不具有创造性。”

paras.en: Applicants can rebut a prima facie case of obviousness by showing the criticality of the range.
paras.zh: 申请人可以通过证明该范围的临界性来反驳表面上的显而易见。

explain.en: China places a narrower range inside a broad prior-art range under selection inventions (Ch. 4 § 4.3(2)): choosing parameters by conventional means without unexpected effects is not inventive. The US words for this are “routine optimization” and “result-effective variable”.
explain.zh: 中国把“宽范围中选出窄范围”放在选择发明（第四章 4.3 节（2））：通过常规手段选择参数且没有预料不到的效果，则不具备创造性。美国对应的说法是 routine optimization（常规优化）和 result-effective variable（影响结果的变量）。

explain.en: Rebuttal words: “criticality”, “unexpected results”, “teaching away”.
explain.zh: 反驳时的关键词：criticality（临界性）、unexpected results（预料不到的效果）、teaching away（教导相反）。

paras.en: A prima facie case of obviousness may be made when chemical compounds have very close structural similarities and similar utilities.
paras.zh: 当化合物结构非常近似且用途相似时，可以构成表面上的显而易见。

paras.en: Compounds which are position isomers (compounds having the same radicals in physically different positions on the same nucleus) or homologs (compounds differing regularly by the successive addition of the same chemical group, e.g., by -CH2- groups) are generally of sufficiently close structural similarity that there is a presumed expectation that such compounds possess similar properties.
paras.zh: 位置异构体（同一母核上相同基团位于不同位置的化合物）或同系物（依次增加同一化学基团、例如 -CH2- 而规则地不同的化合物），通常具有足够近似的结构，可推定其具有相似的性质。

paras.en: A prima facie case of obviousness based on structural similarity is rebuttable by proof that the claimed compounds possess unexpectedly advantageous or superior properties.
paras.zh: 基于结构近似的表面显而易见，可以通过证明要求保护的化合物具有预料不到的有利或更优性质来反驳。

explain.en: China Ch. 10 § 6.1 frames the same question through the three-step test: identify the structural difference, derive the technical problem from the effect of that change, then ask whether the prior art suggested the change. Unexpected use or effect supports inventiveness in both systems.
explain.zh: 中国第十章 6.1 节用三步法处理同一问题：找出结构差异，根据该改造带来的效果确定技术问题，再判断现有技术是否给出这种改造的启示。两国都认可：用途或效果预料不到，支持创造性。

explain.en: US words to know: “lead compound”, “homolog”, “position isomer”, “stereoisomer”, “structural obviousness”.
explain.zh: 需要掌握的美国用语：lead compound（先导化合物）、homolog（同系物）、position isomer（位置异构体）、stereoisomer（立体异构体）、structural obviousness（结构显而易见）。

paras.en: Rebuttal evidence may also include evidence that the claimed invention yields unexpectedly improved properties or properties not present in the prior art.
paras.zh: 反驳证据还可以包括：要求保护的发明产生了预料不到的改进性质，或现有技术所没有的性质。

paras.en: Additionally, the evidence must be reasonably commensurate in scope with the claimed invention.
paras.zh: 此外，证据必须与要求保护的发明范围大致相称。

paras.en: An argument by the applicant is not evidence unless it is an admission, in which case, an examiner may use the admission in making a rejection.
paras.zh: 申请人的论辩本身不是证据，除非它构成自认；这种情况下审查员可以利用该自认作出驳回。

explain.en: “Commensurate in scope” is the US counterpart of China’s rule that post-filing data must prove an effect the skilled person could already derive from the application (Ch. 10 § 3.5.1), plus the general expectation that the effect be shown across what is claimed.
explain.zh: “范围相称”对应中国的相关规则：补交实验数据所证明的效果，应当是本领域技术人员能从申请公开内容中得到的（第十章 3.5.1 节），同时效果应能覆盖所要求保护的范围。

explain.en: Declarations under 37 CFR 1.132 are the US vehicle for such evidence (MPEP § 716).
explain.zh: 美国提交这类证据通常用 37 CFR 1.132 声明（见 MPEP § 716）。

paras.en: I. THE SPECIFICATION MUST INCLUDE A WRITTEN DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION, ENABLEMENT, AND BEST MODE OF CARRYING OUT THE CLAIMED INVENTION
paras.zh: 一、说明书必须包括对发明的书面描述、能够实现的说明，以及实施要求保护的发明的最佳方式

explain.en: Map to China: enablement ≈ Art. 26(3) 充分公开; written description ≈ part of Art. 26(4) 以说明书为依据 plus Art. 33 for amendments; best mode has no Chinese counterpart (and since the AIA it can no longer invalidate an issued patent).
explain.zh: 与中国对应：enablement ≈ 第 26 条第 3 款充分公开；written description ≈ 第 26 条第 4 款“以说明书为依据”的一部分，修改时还对应第 33 条；best mode（最佳方式）中国没有对应规定（AIA 后它也不能再作为宣告专利无效的理由）。

paras.en: To satisfy the written description requirement, a patent specification must describe the claimed invention in sufficient detail that one skilled in the art can reasonably conclude that the inventor had possession of the claimed invention.
paras.zh: 为满足书面描述要求，专利说明书必须足够详细地描述要求保护的发明，使本领域技术人员能够合理地得出发明人已经占有该发明的结论。

paras.en: The fundamental factual inquiry is whether the specification conveys with reasonable clarity to those skilled in the art that, as of the filing date sought, the inventor was in possession of the invention as now claimed.
paras.zh: 根本的事实问题是：说明书是否以合理的清晰度向本领域技术人员表明，在所主张的申请日，发明人已经占有了现在所要求保护的发明。

paras.en: While there is no in haec verba requirement, newly added claims or claim limitations must be supported in the specification through express, implicit, or inherent disclosure.
paras.zh: 虽然不要求逐字记载，但新增的权利要求或限定必须通过明确、隐含或固有的公开在说明书中得到支持。

explain.en: For amendments this is the US counterpart of China Art. 33: China asks whether the content can be “直接地、毫无疑义地确定” from the original documents; the US asks whether the original disclosure shows “possession”. In English OAs: “new matter”, “lacks written description support”.
explain.zh: 用于修改时，这相当于中国第 33 条：中国看能否从原始文件“直接地、毫无疑义地确定”；美国看原始公开是否显示“占有”。英文审查意见常用：new matter（新内容）、lacks written description support（缺乏书面描述支持）。

units.label: MPEP § 2163 (genus claims)
units.title: Genus claims and representative species
units.titleZh: 上位权利要求与代表性下位种

paras.en: A “representative number of species” means that the species which are adequately described are representative of the entire genus.
paras.zh: “代表性数量的下位种”是指，被充分描述的下位种能够代表整个上位范围。

paras.en: Thus, when there is substantial variation within the genus, one must describe a sufficient variety of species to reflect the variation within the genus.
paras.zh: 因此，当上位范围内差异很大时，必须描述足够多样的下位种以反映这种差异。

paras.en: For inventions in an unpredictable art, adequate written description of a genus which embraces widely variant species cannot be achieved by disclosing only one species within the genus.
paras.zh: 对于不可预测领域的发明，只公开一个下位种，不能为涵盖差异很大的下位种的上位范围提供充分的书面描述。

paras.en: Conversely, describing a composition by its function alone typically will not suffice to sufficiently describe the composition.
paras.zh: 反之，仅用功能来描述一种组合物，通常不足以充分描述该组合物。

explain.en: This is how the US polices functional antibody genus claims (AbbVie v. Janssen is cited right here). China handles the same claims mainly under Art. 26(4) support: Part II Ch. 2 § 3.2.1 says a generalization is not supported if there is good reason to doubt that some members solve the problem.
explain.zh: 美国就是用这一条审查功能性限定的抗体上位权利要求（此处引用了 AbbVie v. Janssen）。中国对同类权利要求主要用第 26 条第 4 款“得到说明书支持”：第二部分第二章 3.2.1 节——有充分理由怀疑上位概括中的部分下位不能解决技术问题时，即得不到支持。

explain.en: See also the Amgen v. Sanofi case (enablement) in Leading cases.
explain.zh: 另见「经典判例」里的 Amgen v. Sanofi（能够实现）。

units.label: MPEP § 2164.01
units.title: Test of enablement after Amgen
units.titleZh: Amgen 案后的能够实现标准

paras.en: The standard for determining whether the specification meets the enablement requirement was cast in the Supreme Court decision of Minerals Separation Ltd. v. Hyde, 242 U.S. 261, 270 (1916) which postured the question: is the experimentation needed to practice the invention undue or unreasonable?
paras.zh: 判断说明书是否满足能够实现要求的标准，确立于最高法院 1916 年的 Minerals Separation Ltd. v. Hyde 案，其提出的问题是：实施该发明所需的实验是否过度或不合理？

paras.en: However, “[i]f a patent claims an entire class of processes, machines, manufactures, or compositions of matter, the patent’s specification must enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the entire class….The more one claims, the more one must enable.”
paras.zh: 但是，“如果一项专利要求保护的是一整类方法、机器、制品或组合物，其说明书就必须使本领域技术人员能够制造和使用整个类别……要求保护的越多，需要使其能够实现的也越多。”

explain.en: “The more one claims, the more one must enable” is the sentence to remember from Amgen (2023). The USPTO issued enablement guidelines in January 2024 (89 FR 1563) and kept the Wands factors.
explain.zh: “要求保护的越多，需要使其能够实现的也越多”是 Amgen（2023）最值得记住的一句。USPTO 于 2024 年 1 月发布了能够实现的审查指引（89 FR 1563），继续使用 Wands 因素。

explain.en: China Ch. 2 § 2.1.3 lists the situations where a description cannot be carried out; item (5) — a solution that must be verified by experiment but has no experimental evidence — is the one most used against pharma applications (also Ch. 10 § 3).
explain.zh: 中国第二章 2.1.3 节列举了无法实现的情形；第（5）项——方案必须依赖实验结果证实却没有实验证据——是医药申请中最常用的一项（另见第十章第 3 节）。

units.label: MPEP § 2164.01(a)
units.title: Wands factors
units.titleZh: Wands 因素（是否需要过度实验）

paras.en: (A) The breadth of the claims;
paras.zh: （A）权利要求的宽度；

paras.en: (B) The nature of the invention;
paras.zh: （B）发明的性质；

paras.en: (C) The state of the prior art;
paras.zh: （C）现有技术的状况；

paras.en: (D) The level of one of ordinary skill;
paras.zh: （D）普通技术人员的水平；

paras.en: (E) The level of predictability in the art;
paras.zh: （E）该领域的可预测程度；

paras.en: (F) The amount of direction provided by the inventor;
paras.zh: （F）发明人提供的指导的多少；

paras.en: (G) The existence of working examples; and
paras.zh: （G）是否存在实施例；以及

paras.en: (H) The quantity of experimentation needed to make or use the invention based on the content of the disclosure.
paras.zh: （H）根据公开内容制造或使用该发明所需的实验量。

paras.en: It is improper to conclude that a disclosure is not enabling based on an analysis of only one of the above factors while ignoring one or more of the others.
paras.zh: 只分析上述某一个因素而忽略其他因素，就得出公开不能实现的结论，是不恰当的。

explain.en: When you argue enablement in English, walk through the factors by letter: “Considering the Wands factors, in particular the breadth of the claims (A), the unpredictability of the art (E) and the absence of working examples beyond … (G), undue experimentation would be required.”
explain.zh: 用英文论证能够实现时，按字母逐项分析：Considering the Wands factors, in particular the breadth of the claims (A), the unpredictability of the art (E) and the absence of working examples beyond … (G), undue experimentation would be required.

units.label: MPEP § 2164.08
units.title: Enablement commensurate in scope
units.titleZh: 能够实现的范围应与权利要求相称

paras.en: The focus of the examination inquiry is whether everything within the scope of the claim is enabled.
paras.zh: 审查关注的是：权利要求范围内的一切是否都能够实现。

paras.en: A rejection of a claim under 35 U.S.C. 112 as broader than the enabling disclosure is a 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, enablement rejection and not a 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, definiteness rejection.
paras.zh: 以权利要求宽于能够实现的公开内容为由的驳回，属于 §112(a)（AIA 前为 §112 第一段）的能够实现驳回，而不是 §112(b)（AIA 前为第二段）的清楚性驳回。

explain.en: In China an over-broad claim is usually a 26(4) “not supported” objection rather than 26(3). The US equivalent is a “scope of enablement” rejection (form paragraph ¶ 7.31.03), not indefiniteness.
explain.zh: 在中国，权利要求概括过宽通常提“得不到说明书支持”（26 条 4 款），而不是 26 条 3 款。美国对应的是“能够实现范围”驳回（表格段落 ¶7.31.03），不是不清楚。

paras.en: A decision on whether a claim is indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph requires a determination of whether those skilled in the art would understand what is claimed when the claim is read in light of the specification.
paras.zh: 判断权利要求是否因 §112(b)（AIA 前为第二段）而不清楚，需要确定：本领域技术人员结合说明书阅读权利要求时，是否能理解所要求保护的内容。

paras.en: Such claim construction during prosecution may effectively result in a lower threshold for ambiguity than a court's determination.
paras.zh: 审查阶段的这种权利要求解释，实际上可能导致对含糊不清的门槛低于法院的判断。

paras.en: A claim is indefinite when it contains words or phrases whose meaning is unclear.
paras.zh: 权利要求含有意思不明确的词语时，即为不清楚。

explain.en: The courts apply Nautilus (2014): an issued claim is indefinite if it fails to inform skilled persons about the scope “with reasonable certainty”. China Part II Ch. 2 § 3.2.2 is the counterpart; its examples (“厚”“强”“约”) are classic US § 2173.05(b) “terms of degree” issues.
explain.zh: 法院适用 Nautilus（2014）：已授权的权利要求不能“以合理的确定性”告知技术人员其范围时即为不清楚。中国对应第二部分第二章 3.2.2 节；其中的例子（“厚”“强”“约”）就是美国 § 2173.05(b) 的“程度用语”问题。

explain.en: Also common: “lack of antecedent basis” (§ 2173.05(e)) — “the lever” with no earlier “a lever”. China treats this as a 清楚 issue too.
explain.zh: 另一常见问题：lack of antecedent basis（缺乏引用基础，§ 2173.05(e)）——前面没有 a lever 就写 the lever。中国同样作为“不清楚”处理。

units.label: MPEP § 2173.05(b)
units.title: Relative terms and terms of degree

paras.en: The use of relative terminology in claim language, including terms of degree, does not automatically render the claim indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph.
paras.zh: 在权利要求中使用相对用语（包括程度用语），并不会自动导致权利要求依 §112(b)（AIA 前为第二段）不清楚。

paras.en: Acceptability of the claim language depends on whether one of ordinary skill in the art would understand what is claimed, in light of the specification.
paras.zh: 这类用语是否可接受，取决于本领域普通技术人员结合说明书能否理解所要求保护的内容。

explain.en: China is stricter in wording: Ch. 2 § 3.2.2 says such terms are not allowed “unless” they have an accepted meaning in the field, and “约” is generally not allowed. The US asks whether the specification gives a standard for measuring the degree.
explain.zh: 中国的措辞更严格：第二章 3.2.2 节规定这类用语“不得”使用，除非在该领域有公认确切含义，“约”一般也不允许。美国看说明书是否提供了衡量程度的标准。

paras.en: A claim term is functional when it recites a feature “by what it does rather than by what it is” (e.g., as evidenced by its specific structure or specific ingredients).
paras.zh: 当一个权利要求用语是以“它做什么而不是它是什么”（例如具体结构或具体成分）来记载特征时，该用语就是功能性的。

paras.en: Functional language does not, in and of itself, render a claim improper.
paras.zh: 功能性语言本身并不会使权利要求不当。

explain.en: Functional claims are rarely rejected only as indefinite; the real attack is usually written description or enablement (§§ 2163, 2164). China similarly examines functional features mainly for support (Part II Ch. 2 § 3.2.1).
explain.zh: 功能性权利要求很少仅因不清楚被驳回，真正的问题通常是书面描述或能够实现（§§ 2163、2164）。中国对功能性特征也主要审查是否得到说明书支持（第二部分第二章 3.2.1 节）。

units.label: MPEP § 2106.04(c)
units.title: Products of nature: markedly different
units.titleZh: 自然产物：显著不同的特征

paras.en: The markedly different characteristics analysis is part of Step 2A Prong One, because the courts use this analysis to identify product of nature exceptions.
paras.zh: “显著不同特征”分析属于第 2A 步第一分支，因为法院用这一分析来识别“自然产物”例外。

paras.en: If the claim includes a nature-based product that has markedly different characteristics, then the claim does not recite a product of nature exception and is eligible (Step 2A: NO) at Pathway B unless the claim recites another exception (such as a law of nature or abstract idea, or a different natural phenomenon).
paras.zh: 如果权利要求包含具有显著不同特征的天然来源产品，则该权利要求没有记载自然产物例外，按路径 B 属于可专利客体（第 2A 步：否），除非它记载了其他例外（例如自然规律、抽象概念或另一自然现象）。

explain.en: Chakrabarty (1980) and Myriad (2013) in Leading cases are the source of this test. China has no “markedly different” test: Part II Ch. 10 § 2.1 and § 9.1.2.2 treat isolated natural substances and genes as patentable when first isolated and characterized with industrial use — a big US/China difference for isolated DNA.
explain.zh: 「经典判例」里的 Chakrabarty（1980）和 Myriad（2013）就是这一标准的来源。中国没有“显著不同”标准：第二部分第十章 2.1 节、9.1.2.2 节规定首次分离、表征并有产业利用价值的天然物质和基因可以授权——在分离 DNA 上中美差别很大。

paras.en: (A) The inventions must be independent (see MPEP § 802.01, § 806.06, § 808.01) or distinct as claimed (see MPEP § 806.05 - § 806.05(j)); and
paras.zh: （A）所要求保护的各发明必须彼此独立（见 MPEP §§ 802.01、806.06、808.01）或彼此不同（见 MPEP §§ 806.05–806.05(j)）；并且

paras.en: (B) There would be a serious search and/or examination burden on the examiner if restriction is not required (see MPEP § 803.02, § 808, and § 808.02).
paras.zh: （B）如果不提出限制性要求，审查员在检索和/或审查上将承受严重负担（见 MPEP §§ 803.02、808、808.02）。

paras.en: If the search and examination of all the claims in an application can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine them on the merits, even though they include claims to independent or distinct inventions.
paras.zh: 如果对申请中所有权利要求的检索和审查不会造成严重负担，即使其中包含彼此独立或不同的发明，审查员也必须对它们进行实质审查。

explain.en: US restriction (35 U.S.C. 121) is broader than China’s unity of invention (Art. 31, Part II Ch. 6): the US can split even claims that share a special technical feature, because the test is “independent or distinct + serious burden”. PCT national-stage cases in the US use the unity standard instead.
explain.zh: 美国的限制性要求（35 U.S.C. 121）比中国的单一性（第 31 条，第二部分第六章）宽：即使有相同的特定技术特征也可能被要求限制，因为标准是“独立或不同 + 严重负担”。进入美国国家阶段的 PCT 申请则适用单一性标准。

explain.en: Reply vocabulary: “elect”, “with traverse / without traverse”, “Group I, claims 1–10”, “election of species”, “rejoinder”.
explain.zh: 答复用语：elect（选择）、with traverse / without traverse（有异议/无异议地选择）、Group I, claims 1–10、election of species（物种选择）、rejoinder（重新合并审查）。

paras.en: Second or any subsequent actions on the merits shall be final, except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant’s amendment of the claims, nor based on information submitted in an information disclosure statement filed during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p).
paras.zh: 第二次及以后的实质审查意见应当是最终的，除非审查员提出的新驳回理由既不是申请人修改权利要求所导致的，也不是基于在 37 CFR 1.97(c) 规定期间内连同 37 CFR 1.17(p) 费用提交的信息披露声明（IDS）中的信息。

paras.en: (b) In making such final rejection, the examiner shall repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable to the claims in the application, clearly stating the reasons in support thereof.
paras.zh: （b）作出最终驳回时，审查员应当重复或说明当时认为适用于申请中权利要求的所有驳回理由，并清楚地说明支持理由。

explain.en: A US “final rejection” is not a refusal decision. It closes ordinary prosecution: the applicant can still amend under limited conditions (37 CFR 1.116), file an RCE, or appeal to the PTAB. The Chinese 驳回决定 is closer to the end of the line — the next step is 复审 at the Reexamination and Invalidation Department.
explain.zh: 美国的 final rejection 不是驳回决定，只是结束普通审查程序：申请人仍可有条件地修改（37 CFR 1.116）、提交 RCE 或向 PTAB 上诉。中国的驳回决定更接近终点，下一步是向复审和无效审理部请求复审。

explain.en: China’s counterpart rule on when a refusal may issue is the 听证原则 (Part II Ch. 8 § 6.1.1). Compare the two: the US “new ground of rejection” test versus China’s “驳回所针对的事实改变”.
explain.zh: 中国对应的是何时可以驳回的“听证原则”（第二部分第八章 6.1.1 节）。可以对比：美国看是否“新的驳回理由”，中国看“驳回所针对的事实是否改变”。

paras.en: (b) Prosecution in an application is closed as used in this section means that the application is under appeal, or that the last Office action is a final action (§ 1.113), a notice of allowance (§ 1.311), or an action that otherwise closes prosecution in the application.
paras.zh: （b）本条所称申请的审查程序已结束，是指申请处于上诉中，或者最近一次审查意见是最终审查意见（§1.113）、授权通知（§1.311）或其他结束审查程序的意见。

paras.en: (c) A submission as used in this section includes, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement, an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
paras.zh: （c）本条所称的提交材料包括但不限于：信息披露声明、对说明书、权利要求或附图的修改、新的论点，或支持可专利性的新证据。

explain.en: China has no RCE. The closest idea is that after a 复审 the case may go back to the examiner for continued examination (Part II Ch. 8 § 8). In the US, an RCE keeps the same application number and priority; it is not a new application.
explain.zh: 中国没有 RCE。最接近的是复审后可能回到原审查部门继续审查（第二部分第八章第 8 节）。美国的 RCE 保留同一申请号和优先权，不是新申请。

units.label: MPEP §§ 1204–1205
units.title: Appeal to the PTAB
units.titleZh: 向 PTAB 上诉（单方上诉）

paras.en: (a) PATENT APPLICANT.— An applicant for a patent, any of whose claims has been twice rejected, may appeal from the decision of the primary examiner to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, having once paid the fee for such appeal.
paras.zh: （a）专利申请人——专利申请人的任何一项权利要求被驳回两次的，在缴纳上诉费后，可以就主审查员的决定向专利审判和上诉委员会（PTAB）提出上诉。

paras.en: The usual period of time in which appellant must file his or her brief is 2 months from the date of the notice of appeal.
paras.zh: 上诉人提交上诉理由书的通常期限是自上诉通知之日起 2 个月。

explain.en: “Twice rejected” means any two rejections, not necessarily a final one. Order of steps: notice of appeal → appeal brief → examiner’s answer → (reply brief) → Board decision → CAFC (35 U.S.C. 141) or district court (§ 145). This is ex parte appeal; IPR/PGR are separate inter partes trials at the same Board.
explain.zh: “被驳回两次”是任意两次驳回，不一定要有最终驳回。流程：上诉通知 → 上诉理由书 → 审查员答辩书 →（答复书）→ PTAB 决定 → 联邦巡回上诉法院（35 U.S.C. 141）或地区法院（§145）。这是单方上诉；IPR/PGR 是同一委员会里另外的双方程序。

explain.en: Fee amounts change often (they were adjusted in 2025), so check the USPTO fee schedule rather than the figures printed in MPEP.
explain.zh: 费用经常调整（2025 年刚调过），以 USPTO 现行收费表为准，不要用 MPEP 正文里印的金额。

units.label: MPEP § 2163.03 II
units.title: Relying on a parent application’s filing date

paras.en: Under 35 U.S.C. 120, the claims in a U.S. application are entitled to the benefit of the filing date of an earlier filed U.S. application if the subject matter of the claim is disclosed in the manner provided by 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph in the earlier filed application.
paras.zh: 根据 35 U.S.C. 120，如果权利要求的主题在在先提交的美国申请中按照 §112(a)（AIA 前为第一段）规定的方式公开，则该美国申请中的权利要求可享有在先申请的申请日。

explain.en: Continuations, divisionals and CIPs all rely on this. Each claim gets its own effective date: a CIP claim with new matter only gets the CIP’s own date. China’s 部分优先权 (Part II Ch. 3 § 4.1.4) uses the same claim-by-claim logic.
explain.zh: 继续申请、分案申请和部分继续申请（CIP）都依赖这一条。每项权利要求分别确定有效日：含有新内容的 CIP 权利要求只享有 CIP 自己的申请日。中国的部分优先权（第二部分第三章 4.1.4 节）是同样按权利要求逐项判断的逻辑。
